item.title: Diddy sent to solitary confinement after prison fight with another inmate: multiple reports
item.description: Sean Diddy Combs was reportedly sent to solitary confinement at FCI Fort Dix after a physical altercation with another inmate during his 50-month sentence.
item.content:encoded:
Sean "Diddy" Combs was sent to solitary confinement after he was involved in a fight with another inmate in the prison where he’s serving a 50-month term, according to several reports.

The rapper was convicted last year on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution and is serving his sentence at Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Fort Dix in New Jersey.

The 56-year-old was found guilty a year ago and began serving his sentence at Fort Dix in October.

CASSIE VENTURA FLED THE UNITED STATES AFTER TESTIFYING AGAINST DIDDY IN SEX CRIMES TRIAL: DOCS

The fight started after the other inmate made some kind of comment to the "I’ll Be Missing You" rapper, ABC News reported.

The music mogul "held his own" during the physical fight that was quickly stopped by staff, TMZ reported, citing multiple sources.

It’s unclear if the other inmate was also thrown in solitary as well.

CASSIE VENTURA FLED THE UNITED STATES AFTER TESTIFYING AGAINST DIDDY IN SEX CRIMES TRIAL: DOCS

Combs was moved to the low-security prison after his sentencing because of its drug rehab program and its proximity to his family.

Combs’ high-profile trial last year included testimony from his former girlfriend Casandra "Cassie" Ventura, who claimed he had subjected her to repeated physical abuse, rape and forced sexual encounters involving drugs during their relationship.

A rep for Combs told Fox News Digital he had no comment.

CASSIE VENTURA FLED THE UNITED STATES AFTER TESTIFYING AGAINST DIDDY IN SEX CRIMES TRIAL: DOCS

A representative for the Federal Bureau of Prisons told Fox News Digital: "For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not release information regarding the conditions of confinement for any inmate, including housing assignments, nor do we discuss whether a particular inmate is the subject of allegations, investigations, or sanctions."

Combs is currently scheduled to be released from prison in February 2028, but that could be pushed back due to bad behavior.

item.title: Mike Vrabel untouched by Dianna Russini scandal at first press conference of Patriots training camp
item.description: Mike Vrabel faced zero questions about the Dianna Russini scandal as Patriots players reported for training camp, signaling he may have moved past it.
item.content:encoded:
The drama that shadowed coach Mike Vrabel during the offseason due to his relationship with NFL reporter Dianna Russini was nowhere to be seen Friday when New England Patriots players reported for training camp.

Vrabel must feel he's not only survived but surmounted the ongoing nature of the saga because, well, the thing is not a public topic now as his team gets ready for its first practice on Saturday.

PATRIOTS COACH MIKE VRABEL BREAKS SILENCE ON DIANNA RUSSINI PHOTOS THAT LED TO 'DIFFICULT CONVERSATIONS'

Vrabel, in his second year as the Patriots coach, met with reporters for more than 14 minutes on Friday to kick off the start of camp.

And he fielded not one question about the Russini scandal or anything connected to it.

It was all football – which Vrabel deftly handles like Ted Williams did fastballs back in the day.

Vrabel was asked about the status of second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas, who remains unsigned. Reporters indeed concentrated six of their 20 or so questions to Vrabel on the Jacas topic.

How's the contract negotiations?

How's his health?

Football stuff.

But, again, nothing about the coach and the overriding issue he faced starting April 7 when the New York Post published photographs of him and Russini, then working for The Athletic, enjoying private time at a pool, and in a hot tub, and holding hands and embracing at an Arizona resort before the NFL annual meeting.

Those photos kicked off consistent national coverage that sometimes bordered on cringey – including other photos of the pair at a bar or other events while their spouses were not present. They also predictably led to something of a crisis within the Vrabel family.

Vrabel, in fact, removed himself from the final day of the NFL draft so that he could be with his family and said he was taking time to seek counseling.

But on Friday, nobody asked if the counseling sessions are over or continue.

One would think that if a Super Bowl contender's coach is in counseling, which he made public, someone might wonder if the sessions continue during a hectic training camp.

Or possibly bleed into the season.

Somebody might want to know if Vrabel thinks the counseling succeeded. Or failed. Like, what has changed for Vrabel as a result of those sessions he so publicly announced he was about to undergo?

There was no question to Vrabel at the podium about any of that or anything else having to do with the Russini saga.

We already know Vrabel isn't going to be fired, or even disciplined, for being part of the embarrassment and unwanted attention he brought on himself, the Patriots, and the NFL as a result of this story.

But Friday's presser sealed the fact Vrabel has successfully avoided a major distraction to start training camp.

That actually is his first victory of the season.

Russini, meanwhile, has clearly lost. She resigned from her job at The Athletic and the media company has apparently replaced her with a new so-called insider. She remains at the heart of an internal investigation by the New York Times, which owns The Athletic, with the results of that not yet published.

So barring more facts coming to light, such as the publication of the investigation, Vrabel skates. If he didn't get asked about his counseling sessions and family status on Friday, the chances that happens going forward shrink daily.

So, yes, Vrabel is 1-0 already to kick off training camp.

item.title: Minor league baseball team's fireworks go awry and send fans scrambling for cover in viral video
item.description: Video shows fireworks shooting sideways into the bleachers at CarMax Park during the Richmond Flying Squirrels' postgame pyrotechnics display.
item.content:encoded:
It's a little late in July for a fireworks mishap — those are typically centered around the Fourth of July weekend festivities — but a minor league baseball team's pyro display went sideways in the most literal way imaginable on Thursday.

The Richmond Flying Squirrels — Double-A affiliate of the San Francisco Giants — were hosting a fireworks display on Thursday night after their 3-1 loss to the Hartford Yard Goats.

I think there's a compelling case for benching pre-planned fireworks if you lose, but that's for another time. Despite the L, the Flying Squirrels went ahead with their display over CarMax Park, and the aftermath has been making the rounds on social media.

CANADIAN POLICE POLITELY ASK PEOPLE TO STOP BRINGING THEM UNEXPLODED WWII GRENADES

Now, most importantly, no one was hurt, which is, personally, how I like my fireworks mishaps.

If we're going to have them, let's keep it safe.

Sometimes I see videos of fireworks mishaps, and it can be a little hard to see when something goes wrong, because there's just so much happening.

But in this case, I think we can definitely say that the first sign of a problem was when some of those fireworks started traveling parallel to the ground.

That's suboptimal for many reasons.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

A lot of fans who stuck around to watch some post-game pyro did exactly what I would've done, and that is high-tail it to the relative safety of the concourse. Maybe do a shoulder roll behind a Dippin' Dots cart for safety.

But I'm impressed with how many people didn't move an inch even after fireballs started careening into the bleachers. I wish I had that kind of composure. If one firework went off even remotely off axis, I'd be out in my car before you could say, "Hey, where did that ruggedly handsome gentleman who was sitting right next to us go?"

According to WRIC, the team and the company that put on the show, simply called "Pyro Shows," are investigating what caused the incident.

item.title: ESPN host survives the cuts and then crushes a body-shaming troll, Nick Saban gets mouthy & SEC vs Big Ten
item.description: Alyssa Lang fires back at a body-shaming troll on X after surviving ESPN's roster cuts and thriving as the host at SEC Media Days this week.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Penultimate Friday of July, and the final weekend of the month on tap.

Who has it better than us right now? Nobody. We are ROLLING to close the month. The momentum is there, and it's growing.

ESPN cleaned house this week. Nancy Armour is getting absolutely dragged across the internet. Sophie Cunningham is fighting back. Football practices are underway.

I mean, goodness gracious. What a blessing. What a country. What a time to be alive.

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where ESPN's SEC host Alyssa Lang puts an internet troll in his place after a dominant week at SEC Media Days.

What else? I've got a couple big anniversaries to celebrate today, Nick Saban is back on my TV and it's been wonderful, and Nick Bosa tweeted for the first time in four years specifically to celebrate Ryan Clark's firing.

Amazing.

Grab you a Busch Light like a true patriot, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

It's a Friday. We're gonna keep it light and loose around here. I didn't get to mow the lawn yesterday, so I'm also gonna keep it short because the afternoon thunderstorms are right around the corner and I can't afford to let this jungle go another day.

Before we start, the price of beer at sporting events is truly absurd. Ryan is spot-on with his above analysis saying that Busch Light costs nearly $16 at Wrigley Field.

Frankly, I'm more impressed that Wrigley serves Busch Light. I respect them for that. Didn't think a place like Chicago had that in them. Well done.

That being said, here's your one-month warning that NASCAR returns to Daytona at the end of August and the Busch Light costs $9 in the infield. They also serve it on draft, for those interested (all of you).

God, I love this state. Still pricey, but that's the best you're gonna get at a sporting event in 2026 (non-Augusta).

They also label all of their "domestic drafts" as "American drafts" at Daytona, for those who needed even more of a reason to come on down for the Firecracker 400.

What a track. What a sport.

OK, that's your Ted Talk for the day. Let's get this class started with ESPN's Alyssa Lang not only surviving this week's roster cuts, but then putting a body-shaming internet troll in his place over on Elon's X.

"Just a little off season pudge she’s gonna have to lose if she wants to keep her job."

"Those are actually called abs, in case you haven’t seen your own recently."

Lordy. What a takedown. Alyssa spent the summer traversing Europe, and now she's back in midseason form ready to roll. Been a brutal week at ESPN (all self-inflicted, by the way), but this is the way forward. Alyssa Lang, Tim Tebow, Finebaum, and some SEC football.

All is right with the world. Good to have college football back (sort of). Let's get through these next few weeks and get this season rolling.

Can't wait.

Speaking of college football, Nick Saban returned to our airwaves this week and wasted no time giving Bristol producers a panic attack by letting it rip on live TV with new UF coach Jon Sumrall:

"I’m a Florida resident now, down there amongst the Gators… and I want you to know I’m kind of a semi-Gator. So if you don’t get your s–t together, I’m gonna be in the middle of it."

As one of OutKick's resident Florida fans — along with Austin Perry — Nick is right, by the way. There won't be a ton of patience for Jon Sumrall. Believe me. The Gators have STUNK for years now, and it's been unacceptable.

We don't want to hear about NIL deals and transfers and "trust the process." They need to win — or at least show they can score a freaking touchdown — pretty quickly.

"Two Bits! Four Bits! Six Bits! A Dollar! All for the Gators, stand up and holler!"

OK, let's stick with Saban and rapid-fire this Friday class into a big Friday afternoon of laying down stripes on the yard.

Where do we stand on this comment?

Here's what I know ...

The OutKick audience is overwhelmingly pro-SEC. I know this, because I see the reader emails every day after Ian Miller writes another article dumping on the SEC.

PS: Ian's a good dude, I promise!

I'm also pro-SEC. Duh. I've lived in it my whole life. I agree with Saban when he says the national champion shouldn't automatically define the best conference. Miami very well could have won last year and we all know the ACC ain't good.

But, it's also not the best time for Saban to make this argument given the Big Ten has had the upper hand in recent years. The SEC also went 4-10 in bowl games last season. Not great (at all).

The argument is valid. The timing is ... poor.

Thoughts? Lemme know!

Next? The lefties most-feared NFL player, Nick Bosa, hopped BACK on Twitter with an original tweet for the first time since 2022, and it was a direct shot at Ryan Clark:

Amazing. For those wondering, yes — Nick Bosa hates Ryan Clark. This isn't confirmed, but I'd imagine it stems from when Clark went on his awful podcast and cried because Bosa wore a MAGA hat during an NBC postgame interview:

"When you say Make America Great ... Again ... what was so great about it before? What part of America are you trying to get to?"

Goodness. What a loser. Frankly, it's stunning it took ESPN this long to cut ties. Good riddance, Rhino!

OK, that's it for today — and this week. I leave you all with two very special anniversaries on the way out.

First? This week marks six years since we started the insufferable COVID baseball season with Dr. Fauci throwing, easily, the worst first pitch in the history of baseball.

Second? TODAY is the 26-year anniversary of Varitek and A-Rod throwing hands in arguably the most consequential baseball fight of all time.

I remember watching it live like it was yesterday. We were on vacation at our old cabin in North Carolina. I was mesmerized. It's when I truly became a Red Sox fan.

item.title: CNN host admits he was wrong to say illegal immigrant voting 'never happens' after New Jersey error
item.description: Michael Smerconish says he can no longer claim noncitizen voting never happens after New Jersey revealed a software error registered 6,600 noncitizens.
item.content:encoded:
CNN and SiriusXM host Michael Smerconish acknowledged Wednesday on "The Michael Smerconish Program" that he could no longer claim noncitizen voting never occurred after New Jersey disclosed that a software error improperly registered roughly 6,600 noncitizens and fewer than 400 cast ballots.

"I can’t say that any longer," Smerconish said. "I don’t know how often it does happen, but I can’t say any longer, ‘This never happens.’"

Smerconish said he had previously reached the opposite conclusion after discussing a January New York Times analysis titled "Initial Review Finds No Widespread Illegal Voting by Migrants, Puncturing a Trump Claim." The analysis found no evidence of widespread fraud but noted that noncitizens sometimes appeared on voter rolls.

Smerconish said the New Jersey disclosure would give President Donald Trump and his allies a lasting response when opponents disputed that noncitizen voting occurred.

GOP ERUPTS OVER 6,600 NONCITIZEN VOTERS FOUND IN BLUE STATE AS SCANDAL DEEPENS: ‘WORSE THAN ANYONE EXPECTED’

"'Well, what about New Jersey?' See, it actually does happen," Smerconish said, in a clip flagged by Mediaite.

Political analyst Mark Halperin agreed that the disclosure undercut categorical claims about noncitizen voting while cautioning that more information was needed before conclusions could be reached about its scale.

"Based on what we now know, the thing that Democrats said doesn’t happen happened," Halperin said. "And it’s not right to take the word of the Democratic governor of New Jersey about what actually happened."

Halperin called for an independent investigation into how the registrations occurred, whether the same problem appeared elsewhere and whether New Jersey’s estimate captured the full extent of the error.

WATCH: TRUMP DOJ VOWS TO PURSUE ‘EVERY SINGLE’ VOTING VIOLATION AFTER NJ ROLL SHOCKER

"If it happened by accident on this small scale, it requires a lot more explanation and investigation about whether it’s happened in New Jersey more or elsewhere," Halperin said. "But the scale is not very significant. So we need to know more."

Fox News Digital reached out to New Jersey Gov. Mike Sherrill for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Sherrill said the error affected people who indicated they were not U.S. citizens while applying for driver's licenses or identification cards between June 2023 and June 2024. The system nevertheless registered them to vote.

"Our preliminary analysis shows fewer than 400 individuals who were newly registered for the first time because of the error voted," Sherrill said. "They were registered as Democrats, Republicans and Unaffiliated voters and were scattered across the state."

NEW JERSEY REMOVES 6,600 PEOPLE FROM VOTER ROLLS WHO WERE ELIGIBLE TO CAST A BALLOT FOR 2024 ELECTION

Sherrill ordered the affected registrations removed, launched an investigation and began replacing IDEMIA, the vendor involved with the Motor Vehicle Commission system. She blamed failures under former Democratic Gov. Phil Murphy's administration.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"This failure didn’t occur under my watch, but accountability starts now," Sherrill said.

IDEMIA disputed efforts to place responsibility solely on the company, telling Fox News Digital that New Jersey election officials were responsible for determining eligibility.

"The voter registration information is transmitted to the New Jersey Department of State, Division of Elections, which is ultimately responsible for verifying eligibility to vote," IDEMIA said.

The Justice Department subsequently demanded information about the 6,600 registrations and the fewer than 400 people who voted. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon gave the state five days to provide names, registration details and voting records.

"Ensuring that U.S. citizens’ votes are not illegally diluted by noncitizens’ votes is of paramount importance," Dhillon said.

item.title: Republicans target Trump's crypto empire with new plan, Dems say it falls short
item.description: Trump's income surged 250% to $2.2 billion largely from crypto ventures, but Senate Democrats say the Clarity Act's ethics provisions fall short.
item.content:encoded:
Senate Republicans want to rein in President Donald Trump’s income explosion since returning to the White House, but Democrats aren’t sold on how they’re going to do it.

The Senate is on the cusp of moving landmark cryptocurrency legislation known as the Clarity Act that, if passed, proponents say would finally fold the novel currency into the nation’s web of financial regulations.

Tucked away in the over 600-page package are a slate of ethics provisions that target Trump, the vice president and their spouses. The White House signed off on the provisions, and the architects of the bill say that the restrictions reach beyond just Trump and target lawmakers, too.

GOP RIFT GROWS AS THUNE HITS BRAKES ON TRUMP'S ELECTION BILL TO AVERT SHUTDOWN

But for now, it’s not enough for Senate Democrats.

"Someone can call it an ethics provision," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said. "But if it doesn't stop the president from profiting off of crypto, and using it as a way to take bribes right out in public. Then it's not really any expedition.

The list of guardrails included preventing federal officials from creating their own digital currency for profit, promoting or endorsing crypto, creating a divestiture or blind trust requirement one year after enactment, allowing officials to own crypto and a disclosure of crypto sales.

Sen. Cynthia Lummis, R-Wyo., who has led the effort on the Clarity Act, told Fox News’ Maria Bartiromo that the idea isn’t to "plan legislation around one person who holds one office for the next two years, but rather, over time, that will serve the House, the Senate, the judiciary, and the executive branch in a fair way."

HOUSE GOP VOTES TO PUNT GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN BATTLE TO AFTER NOVEMBER MIDTERMS

"The struggle is, of course, a lot of Democrats are absolutely focused on one person, and that's President Trump," Lummis said. "So since President Trump actually agreed that he would have the choice to either put his assets in a blind trust, or divest of his participation in digital assets and companies that derive revenue from digital assets, somehow, that's not enough."

There are other gripes with the package, but the ethics provisions are proving a sharp red line. That’s because Trump’s income between 2024 and 2025 erupted by about 250% — from just over $620 million to about $2.2 billion.

And much of that increase is attributed to his various holdings and ventures in crypto, which are run by his sons, Don Jr. and Eric, according to the president’s financial disclosure forms reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Trump’s income shot up by $1.4 billion during his first year in office thanks to earnings from the $TRUMP memecoin, World Liberty Financial token sales and Stablecoin Holdco, among others.

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, who alongside Sen. Cynthia Lummis, R-Wyo., worked with the White House to draft the ethics provisions, said that the "behavior" that was being targeted was issuance, promotion, and sponsorship of crypto.

"Again, a very different standard than Nancy Pelosi was held to," Moreno said.

REPUBLICAN SAYS TRUMP'S TOP ELECTION PRIORITY 'DEAD' IN SENATE AS GOP FRACTURES AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

When asked about Democrats already raising issues with the provisions, Moreno told Fox News Digital, "They're always obsessed with putting things into the base bill, just offer an amendment."

"That’s the way this place was built, you know, let's put the base bill out there," he said. "The ethics piece is this much of the bill — Tiny bit — just offer an amendment."

Democrats have noted that the ethics provisions don’t specifically target his sons, meaning that the Trump family crypto empire, which has heavily benefited from his name and time in office, would be left largely unchecked.

They also put sole enforcement power into the hands of Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, a close ally of Trump’s, and are set to sunset on Jan. 20, 2029, when Trump will have left office.

Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., told Fox News Digital that he still has "a lot of ethics concerns, and there’s still work to do."

"This is the partisan draft. It's very obviously not going anywhere," Booker said. "If there's only one pathway to do this it’s doing (it in) a bipartisan manner. There are enough of us on both sides of the aisle that we should be able to land this. It's good faith negotiations."

The objections to the bill, for now, appear to be slowing its roll through the Senate as the upper chamber sprints to a monthlong break in August, and deals with a shrinking window of opportunity to finish legislation before the year is out.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., had hoped to get the Clarity Act on the floor next week, but acknowledged that might not be possible.

"I don’t think we’ll be able to get it done, but I would like to at least get Clarity started," he said.

item.title: DNC panel picks first 2028 primary state after battle over key voting blocs
item.description: The DNC Rules and Bylaws panel voted to keep South Carolina as the first 2028 Democratic primary, choosing it over Nevada in a battle over voter outreach.
item.content:encoded:
South Carolina is on course to remain the lead-off primary in the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nominating calendar, after landing a key party committee's recommendation.

The Democratic National Committee's (DNC) powerful Rules and Bylaws panel, meeting in the nation's capital on Friday, picked South Carolina over Nevada to hold the party's first presidential nominating contest in 2028, a move that will likely maintain a key role in the primary calendar for Black voters, who are a crucial part of the Democrats' base.

The vote comes after intense lobbying by both states, as well as by New Hampshire, and Iowa over the past year to hold the much-coveted lead-off Democratic primary in the race for the White House. And the battle between South Carolina and Nevada was seen as a struggle between rewarding Black voters, who have long been loyal Democratic voters, and outreach to Latino voters, with whom President Donald Trump and Republicans made major gains in the 2024 election, handing Democrats major setbacks.

The panel also voted to allow Nevada, New Hampshire, Michigan, Virginia, and New Mexico to hold primaries in the early voting window, before the rest of the states hold nominating contests starting ahead of Super Tuesday.

WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN: CHECK OUT THE FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS ON THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

According to the panel, South Carolina would hold its primary on Jan. 22, 2028, with Nevada going second on Feb. 1, 2028, followed by New Hampshire on Feb. 8, 2028. New Mexico would hold the fourth contest, on Feb. 15, 2028, followed by Michigan on Feb. 22, 2028, and Virginia on Feb. 29, 2028.

The Rules and Bylaws Committee's proposals on the calendar will face a final vote by the DNC's entire membership when the party holds its summer meeting next month in Austin, Texas.

Minyon Moore, the panel's co-chair, said that South Carolina "will emerge as the first contest."

South Carolina supporters pointed to the recent Supreme Court ruling that weakened the Voting Rights Act, and the ongoing redistricting battles, and argued that the party needs to reaffirm its commitment to Black voters when their electoral strength has been diminished.

Nevada allies, meanwhile, pointed to the western battleground state's diverse electorate of Latino, Black, Asian American and Pacific Islanders, and its working class population as the ideal state for Democratic White House hopefuls to make their case.

New Hampshire held the lead-off presidential primary for both Democrats and Republicans for a century, and while the GOP adhered to tradition in the last race for the White House, the DNC upended its calendar, placing South Carolina ahead of the Granite State. The move was seen as an unwanted distraction for Democrats during the 2024 primaries.

AOC SURGES PAST BUTTIGIEG, LEAVES HARRIS IN THE DUST: NEW POLL IN KEY 2028 PRIMARY STATE

National Democrats for years had knocked both Iowa — whose caucuses for 50 years led off the party’s nominating calendar until 2024 — and New Hampshire as unrepresentative of the party as a whole because the states have largely white populations with few major urban areas. Nevada and South Carolina, which are much more diverse than either Iowa or New Hampshire, were added near the top of the Democratic calendar two decades ago to increase the diversity of the early states’ electorate

.

New Hampshire Democrats have long pushed back, saying the state’s rich tradition of grassroots, retail politics, its well-informed electorate, its high percentage of voter participation and its longtime status as a key general election swing state make it the perfect locale to hold the first-in-the-nation primary.

After the DNC removed New Hampshire from the top of its 2024 calendar, putting the state second along with Nevada, the Granite State still moved to the head of the line. Adhering to a half-century-old law that mandates the Granite State to hold the first presidential primary a week ahead of any similar contest, New Hampshire Secretary of State Dave Scanlan scheduled the Democratic and GOP presidential primary contests for Jan. 23, 2024.

The Democratic contest, which was held before South Carolina and Nevada, ended up being an unsanctioned election, with the DNC banning the state's delegates from attending that summer's nominating convention. The DNC later made peace with New Hampshire and reinstated their convention delegates.

But this time around, the party is proposing much more lethal sanctions against states that go rogue, as well as tough penalties on candidates who campaign in those states, in hopes of preventing unsanctioned contests.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Because of this calendar, our candidates will be tested," said DNC Chair Ken Martin. "Because of this process, millions more Americans will be heard. Because of this committee, our party is and will be stronger. And because of the work that all of us have done together, our eventual nominee will enter the general election, prepared to unite our coalition to compete in every part of the country and to win back the White House."

But longtime New Hampshire Democratic Party Chair Ray Buckley, in a statement after the vote on the calendar, argued, "Today’s vote shows that many party insiders have learned nothing from 2024. New Hampshire has a proven track record of testing our candidates with a rigorous, fair, and efficient process, yet those qualities did not prevail. This committee’s vote does not change the realities governing New Hampshire’s primary, which are beyond the control of both this committee and our state party."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Nevada Democratic Party Chair Daniele Monroe-Moreno emphasized in a statement, "As an early state and the first true test of a candidate’s ability to win in a general election, we will play a critical role in the nomination process."

While Democrats have argued over their 2028 calendar, the rival Republican National Committee announced earlier this year that their nominating schedule, with Iowa and New Hampshire as the lead-off contests, would be unchanged.

item.title: Spiny lobster mini season kicks off in Florida, drawing eager divers to the water
item.description: Florida's spiny lobster mini season arrives the last Wednesday and Thursday of July, and here's what you need to know about limits and permits.
item.content:encoded:
Summer is in full swing in South Florida, but if you've been down here at any point in the last few months or you own a thermometer, you're probably aware of that.

With the calendar rapidly approaching the last week in July, it's easy to get down about summer coming to an end, but it also means we are closing in on the most wonderful time of the year.

No, I'm not talking about Christmas. It's spiny lobster mini season here in the Sunshine State.

TWO REGULAR JOES WILL COMPETE WITH PROS FOR $3.25M PURSE AT INAUGURAL 'THE CHAMPIONS' BASS FISHING TOURNAMENT

If you're unfamiliar with mini season, it's basically a time where commercial fishers aren't allowed to catch any lobsters so that anyone who does so recreationally can have first dibs.

It happens the last Wednesday and Thursday of July every year, and every hotel along the Florida Keys braces in anticipation for the mass pilgrimage of both natives and visitors who will make the trek down to participate.

For those who wish to partake in the wonders of mini season, there are some rules you must follow.

You are limited to 12 lobsters per person per day, unless you are diving in Monroe County (home of the Florida Keys). If you're staying there, your limit is six per person per day.

Also, keep an eye out for protected areas and National and State Parks, as those are obviously no-take zones.

In addition to the limit, you must also make sure the carapace (the part from its head to the beginning of the tail) exceeds 3 inches in length. You must also have a lobster permit, which you can easily obtain by going to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's website.

After all that is taken care of, the fun really begins.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

I'm not even a big fan of eating lobster at a restaurant, but I have happily devoured pounds of Florida spiny lobster that my friends and family have caught while staying in The Keys.

Much like with fish, you will never have a more delicious lobster than the one you caught yourself.

One of the beauties of diving for lobster during mini season is that you don't need any fancy gear to have a great time, either.

Sure, it helps to have dive tanks and SCUBA gear, but plenty of spots along the Gulf waters are shallow enough - particularly in the Upper and Middle Keys - that all you need is a mask, snorkel, a pair of gloves, and a kayak to hit your daily limit.

The lobsters love to hide in little holes, crevices, and even underneath old sunken personal items, so be sure to leave no stone unturned (literally).

I would recommend staying the whole week even though the actual season is only from Wednesday through Thursday so that you can partake in the other activity that area is famous for: fishing.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

When you aren't out diving for lobster, there is plenty of world class fishing to be done all up and down both coasts of the Florida Keys.

As a native Floridian, my summers never feel complete without taking the journey down to our state's most famous archipelago in late July, and I'm hoping some of you are able to experience that magic for yourselves.

Summer is all about creating memories that last a lifetime, and I can't think of a better place to create some new ones than the Florida Keys during spiny lobster mini season.

item.title: 5 options to replace Ryan Clark on ESPN's Super Bowl halftime show
item.description: Kurt Warner, Steve Smith Sr., Dan Orlovsky and Mina Kimes are among five candidates to replace Ryan Clark on ESPN's Super Bowl halftime show.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest-picture takeaway from ESPN's decision to part ways with Ryan Clark is that it opens a seat on the network's coverage of its first-ever Super Bowl this February.

Clark was one of three analysts on "Monday Night Countdown," which is expected to serve as ESPN's official Super Bowl pregame and halftime show. Jason Kelce and Marcus Spears are the other analysts, while Scott Van Pelt is expected to return as host.

From ESPN's perspective, the timing makes sense. The Super Bowl halftime show could draw more than 140 million viewers. The network could not allow Clark to represent the brand during its biggest broadcast ever, given his history of bigoted remarks.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

So, here are five possible replacements for ESPN:

Of the internal candidates, Kurt Warner makes the most sense.

As part of ESPN's acquisition of NFL Network assets, the company now has access to Warner. He would give the network a Hall of Fame quarterback on the panel, something that has traditionally been a staple of major NFL studio shows.

Troy Aikman is the only other Hall of Fame quarterback on ESPN's roster, but he'll be in the booth calling the game.

One logistical hurdle remains. Warner currently serves as the lead analyst for Westwood One's "Monday Night Football" radio broadcasts, including the Super Bowl.

Sources tell OutKick ESPN could use Warner on the pregame show because he's already on site each week for the radio broadcast. He would have to step away from his Westwood One duties, however, to serve as ESPN's halftime analyst.

As WFAN host Craig Carton argued this week, Warner would almost certainly choose television over radio, if he's able to get out of his contract. Whether that's possible remains unclear.

Steve Smith Sr. is another analyst ESPN inherited from NFL Network.

Interestingly, Smith could also assume some of Clark's day-to-day responsibilities. Sources say he impressed ESPN decision makers during appearances on "First Take" around the NFL Draft. With the network planning to better separate the guest lineups between "First Take" and "Get Up" this season, Smith could earn a regular role on one or both shows.

That also makes him a logical candidate for "Monday Night Countdown."

Dan Orlovsky is ESPN's best daily NFL analyst and would give the panel a former quarterback.

He's also the opposite of Ryan Clark in one important respect. Few personalities at ESPN are less likely to drift away from football and into unrelated topics than Orlovsky is. Such decision-making is underrated.

Orlovsky has become one of the network's more recognizable NFL voices through "NFL Live," "Get Up," "First Take," and "The Pat McAfee Show."

Scheduling may be the biggest obstacle. Last season, Orlovsky stayed in New York on Mondays for "Get Up" and "First Take" instead of traveling with NFL Live to the Monday Night Football site.

ESPN may decide he's more valuable anchoring its morning lineup, especially after moving on from Cam Newton. Orlovsky and his representatives could just as easily argue for a schedule that allows him to do both, by moving his morning show responsibilities to later in the week.

USA TODAY WRITER SAYS CAITLIN CLARK PUTS BLACK AND QUEER WNBA PLAYERS 'IN DANGER' BY FLOPPING

To be clear, we're not suggesting ESPN should choose Mina Kimes as its Super Bowl halftime analyst. We think that would be a mistake.

However, we'd be surprised if her name isn't, at least, mentioned internally.

Because some critics have predictably accused ESPN of racism for moving on from Clark, it's possible executives feel pressure to make a symbolic personnel move. Kimes would almost certainly be part of that discussion.

Choosing someone who never played or coached in the NFL for ESPN's first Super Bowl halftime show, however, would erase much of the goodwill the network has built with football fans over the past few days.

Another option is simply moving one of ESPN's Sunday pregame shows to Mondays, be it Randy Moss, Alex Smith, Rex Ryan, and Tedy Bruschi.

Each would be an upgrade over Clark, and by a substantial margin. Moss is the biggest star from his playing career. Bruschi is the strongest television analyst of the four.

There's another possibility worth considering.

Networks carrying the Super Bowl often supplement their studio coverage with active players whose seasons have ended during the postseason. Given how much emphasis ESPN is placing on its first Super Bowl, don't be surprised if the network adds a major current or recently retired player alongside its existing crew, even if just for the one broadcast.

Names like Matthew Stafford, Jameis Winston, Kirk Cousins, or Joe Flacco come to mind.

Or, perhaps for a one-time appearance, ESPN could pair Jason Kelce with his brother, Travis Kelce, who is expected to retire at the end of the Chiefs' season.

item.title: Georgia high school shooting suspect Colt Gray changes plea to guilty, now faces life in prison
item.description: Colt Gray, the suspect in the 2024 shooting at Apalachee High School in Georgia, now faces life in prison after entering a guilty plea on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
The 16-year-old charged with killing two students and two teachers during a 2024 shooting at Apalachee High School in Georgia now faces life in prison after he entered a guilty plea Friday.

Colt Gray, who previously pleaded not guilty last October, entered the new plea Friday without reaching a deal with prosecutors. Gray, who was 14 at the time of the shooting, was charged as an adult with 55 total counts, including murder in the four deaths and 25 counts of aggravated assault. His trial had been scheduled to start in mid-October.

Teachers Richard "Ricky" Aspinwall, 39, and Cristina Irimie, 53, and students Mason Schermerhorn and Christian Angulo, both 14, died in the September 2024 shooting in Barrow County, about 45 miles northeast of Atlanta. Another teacher and eight more students were wounded, seven of them hit by gunfire.

Shayna Aspinwall, Richard Aspinwall's wife, told the judge on Friday that the "grief of losing him is constant" and lamented that the lives of their daughters, who were 2 and 5 when their father died, will be "forever marked by his absence."

FATHER OF GEORGIA HIGH SCHOOL SHOOTING SUSPECT CONVICTED OF SECOND-DEGREE MURDER, INVOLUNTARY MANSLAUGHTER

Breanna Schermerhorn, whose son Mason was killed, told the judge she does not forgive Colt Gray. She said that while adults around him missed multiple warning signs, he was the one who decided to bring a gun to school and to pull the trigger.

"Those decisions were his and his alone," she said.

She described her son as someone who "made people that were typically unseen feel seen, accepted and safe" and said she was confident he would have befriended Colt Gray if he'd had the chance.

"Mason deserved a future and we all deserved a future with Mason in it, and Colt took that from Mason and everyone who loved him," she said. She and two of Mason's sisters asked the judge for a sentence of life without parole.

Before accepting the plea, Barrow County Superior Court Judge Nicholas Primm asked Gray a series of questions meant to ensure that the teenager was aware of the consequences of his plea and was entering it voluntarily. To each question, Gray responded, "Yes, your honor."

NEW VIDEO SHOWS OKLAHOMA HIGH SCHOOL PRINCIPAL TACKLING GUNMAN WHO OPENED FIRE INSIDE THE SCHOOL

Because he pleaded guilty to murder, Gray faces a minimum sentence of life in prison, according to The Associated Press. The judge must decide whether he should be eligible for parole after hearing victim statements, evidence and each side's summary of the case.

Gray sat at a table in the courtroom with his feet chained together next to his attorney. Members of the community, including some victims and family members, were present in the courtroom.

A jury in March convicted his father, Colin Gray, of charges including second-degree murder and involuntary manslaughter, and he is scheduled to be sentenced next week.

Prosecutors successfully argued that Colin Gray provided his son with the AR-15-style rifle used in the attack as a Christmas gift, continued buying him ammunition, despite being aware of his mental health deterioration and prior school shooting threats investigated by law enforcement.

The prosecution told jurors that despite those concerns, Gray did not pursue inpatient treatment for his son.

Fox News Digital’s Michael Dorgan and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: The 76ers jump to betting favorite out East after LeBron James takes his talents to Philadelphia
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers jumped past the New York Knicks as Eastern Conference betting favorites after signing LeBron James to a two-year, $8 million deal.
item.content:encoded:
Love him or hate him, LeBron James is still a needle-mover. At least in the sportsbooks and prediction markets.

After signing LeBron to a team-friendly two-year, $8 million deal, the Philadelphia 76ers are now the betting favorite in the Eastern Conference to win the 2027 championship at Kalshi.

I know the percentages can be confusing, so in American odds, the Sixers are +684 to win the title next season. They passed the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks, who are the second-betting favorite (+1240) out East as of 2 p.m. ET Friday, July 24.

LEBRON JAMES MAKES NBA FREE AGENCY DECISION, ANNOUNCES PLANS TO SIGN WITH 76ERS

This is the second huge move Philly has made this offseason, coming off the heels of trading Paul George to the Boston Celtics for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown.

Now, Philadelphia's starting five includes LeBron, Brown, 2022-23 NBA MVP Joel Embiid, two-time All-Star guard Tyrese Maxey, and SG V.J. Edgecombe, who finished third in Rookie of the Year voting last season.

Ultimately, the question: Is this team good enough to win a title?

I mean, if the 76ers get insane injury luck in the playoffs, of course they can win a championship. Every team can. And in an NBA2K-sense: Sure. If you turn off injuries and control the players yourself.

Whether the personalities and playing styles mesh is another conversation. In fact, there's a solid chance the 2026-27 Philadelphia 76ers will be a too many cooks in the kitchen type thing.

In theory, upgrading from PG to Brown, while adding LeBron to a Sixers squad that upset the Celtics in the first round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs (which led Boston to spazz and make a franchise-altering trade), is a power move.

CELTICS AGREE TO SEND JAYLEN BROWN, 2024 FINALS MVP, TO 76ERS IN BLOCKBUSTER NBA TRADE: REPORT

Brown is a champion and five-time NBA All-Star who averaged career-bests in points, rebounds and assists last season. He is in his athletic prime and has never suffered a significant injury.

Again, love him or hate him, LeBron balled last season, his final with the Los Angeles Lakers. He averaged 20.9 points on 51.5% shooting with 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists in 60 games.

But LeBron has always been ball-dominant, and I don't see him changing much at 41, soon-to-be 42-years-old. Brown is an iso-scorer who likes to take defenders off the dribble and operates in the mid-range.

Philadelphia needs Embiid healthy and playing at 70% of his MVP-self to justify being the betting favorite in the East. However, Embiid always gets hurt, and he is a much worse defender than he was when in his prime.

Maxey actually led the 76ers in scoring last season despite Embiid having the highest usage rate on the team. Are we sure he'll be okay with giving the ball up to LeBron and Brown?

Deferring isn't the same as buying into a lesser role and still playing your a-- off. It isn't guaranteed that two or three All-Stars will be cool with being essentially role players, and you need "glue guys" to win a title.

That said, Philly should be second to New York as the betting favorite to win the East. The Knicks will have the same starting five in their title defense, all of whom are in their athletic primes. If they met in the playoffs, Jalen Brunson would be the best player on the floor.

item.title: Paul Anka slams modern singers, says Frank Sinatra would have 'thrown a chair'
item.description: Paul Anka says Frank Sinatra would have thrown a chair if asked to use autotune, praising an era when singers had to perform live until perfect.
item.content:encoded:
Paul Anka slammed modern singers and the technology that helps them sound better, saying Franka Sinatra would have thrown a chair at someone if they asked him to use autotune.

Anka called Sinatra and Elvis Presley his two "towers" of music while speaking to Billy Corgan of the Smashing Pumpkins on his "The Magnificent Others" podcast this week.

"When Elvis was around, he just – they both owned a room, and they were both given that it factor," he explained.

FRANK SINATRA'S DESERT HIDEAWAY WAS 'ALL SEX, ALL THE TIME,' FORMER VALET CLAIMS

He added, "And Elvis worked his a-- off. This was a shy guy. I would sit with him like this: ‘Hey, Paulie,’" he said in a reserved imitation of Presley. "‘How you doing, man? Yeah, Paul. You know, one day I'm going to do that "My Way." I love that "My Way."’"

He said he told Presley that he wouldn’t want to cover the song made famous by Sinatra because it wasn’t exactly his style of music.

"But what an amazing force to watch and be around it," he continued.

The "Put Your Head on My Shoulder" singer said he and Presley learned that it "wasn't about just getting up there and singing. You had to entertain people."

The 84-year-old gave the example of the notoriously unpredictable Bob Dylan, whom he admits he loves, but said would sometimes go on stage and "couldn’t give a s--- and people walk out, ‘What the f---?’ If you don't entertain people, you're dead."

Regarding Sinatra, he vowed the "Fly Me to the Moon" crooner "will get bigger, young people will learn exactly what true quality is, you know, at a time when there was no autotune."

"Think about the difference. I don't know who the f--- is doing the singing today. Do you?" he admitted. "Can you imagine back then if you said to Sinatra, ‘We're going to give you an autotune’? He would have thrown a chair at you."

Singers in Sinatra’s time, he said, "walked in a studio after rehearsing, as I stated earlier, and you kept singing, and that band kept playing till you got perfect."

"That was it," he continued. "And he was the guy."

Anka said Sinatra set the standard and "made it tough for anybody to ever stand in front of a band again. We all came second, but he was the guy we emulated."

He also said that Sammy Davis, Jr. was the most "short-changed" on being recognized.

"To Frank and Dean [Martin] and to all of us, he was the most talented," Anka said.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"That was the most talented guy," he professed. "He was a musician. He played drums. He played this, he did that. He sang great. He was the guy that I hope today somehow they put him back in the forefront. And Dean was an underrated singer."

Anka said a specific song that he wrote for Davis but didn't name was "as important to me as ‘My Way’ with Sinatra."

Anka wrote "My Way" for Sinatra in 1968.

He also praised Michael Jackson’s talent, saying, "I never worked with anyone like that … I knew the kid was so talented."

item.title: Man accused of raping three underage girls faces new charge from prison
item.description: Imarr Finley, facing rape charges involving three underage girls in Harrisburg, now faces vandalism charges after allegedly breaking a Dauphin County Prison window.
item.content:encoded:
A man awaiting trial for allegedly raping three underage girls is facing new charges after reportedly breaking a window inside a Pennsylvania prison.

Imarr Finley, 25, of Harrisburg, Pa., has been at the jail since December 2024, when he was arrested after allegedly kidnapping a 12-year-old girl on her way home from school, taking her to his home and raping her, according to court records obtained by Pennlive.com.

Court records show Finley was charged with the rape of two other girls. One girl was 17, while the other was 13 or 14, Pennlive.com reported.

Finley's most recent criminal charge stems from a July 8 incident when he allegedly broke a control room window on the Dauphin County Prison's P block while he was out of his cell on recreation time, according to a probable cause affidavit obtained by Pennlive.com.

FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES

The affidavit, filed by the Dauphin County District Attorney’s Office, claimed two corrections officers saw Finley break the window, which caused $772 in damage.

Court records show Finley was charged on Thursday with institutional vandalism, a second-degree misdemeanor.

For that charge, he was arraigned on Thursday afternoon and a preliminary hearing has been scheduled for Aug. 4. Fox News Digital reached out to the prison for comment.

The first alleged rape occurred on Nov. 25, 2024, in the uptown Harrisburg area, according to police.

According to Pennlive.com, the girl told authorities that a man dressed in all black and a mask over his face was following her.

FORMER PRISON GUARD WHO HAD SEX TAPE WITH INMATE GO VIRAL IS FILLED WITH REGRET & NOW FOCUSING ON BEING A MOM

The man, who police say was Finley, got the girl to follow him to his house, where he allegedly raped her and threatened the girl's family if she told anyone, Pennlive.com reported. Days later, on Dec. 4, 2024, Finley was arrested by Harrisburg police after he fled out the second story window of a home and tried to flee by running across rooftops, according to authorities.

On March 23, 2026, Finley was charged in connection with the rape of a 13- or 14-year-old girl who he allegedly lured to his house with a fake Snapchat photo, Pennlive.com reported.

Four days later, he was charged with raping a 17-year-old girl after authorities said DNA evidence tied him to the crime, according to the outlet.

Finley is being held without bond and is due to appear in court for the rape charges on July 30.

item.title: Tony Romo arrested in Milwaukee for alleged OWI offense: report

item.content:encoded:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo was arrested in Milwaukee on Thursday night for allegedly operating while intoxicated.

Romo was reportedly stopped on a highway and performed poorly on field sobriety tests, FOX6 in Milwaukee reported. He was released and is due in court Sept. 21.

Other information regarding the arrest was not immediately available. Neither the Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office nor CBS immediately responded to emails from Fox News Digital.

Romo retired from football in 2017 and soon joined CBS as a color commentator.

He was the Cowboys' starter from 2006 to 2015, but an injury cost him his spot in 2016 to Dak Prescott. The Cowboys released him after the season, and he eventually hung up the cleats.

Romo threw for 34,183 yards, 248 touchdowns, and 117 interceptions, completing 65.3% of his passes. 

He was named to the Pro Bowl four times and finished tied for third in the MVP vote in 2014 behind Aaron Rodgers and J.J. Watt — he was tied with DeMarcio Murray.

SAQUON BARKLEY 'CAN UNDERSTAND' BACKLASH FOR HIS TRUMP HANGOUT, 'GLAD' GIANTS STARS WORKED OUT DIFFERENCES

item.title: Platner campaign strategist admits tattoo, Reddit posts should have been 'enough' to disqualify him
item.description: Graham Platner strategist Morris Katz said in a new interview that the candidate's Reddit posts and troubling behavior should have disqualified him from the Maine Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
Graham Platner's lead campaign strategist, Morris Katz, admitted on Friday that the controversies that came out about the ex-Maine Democratic Senate candidate early on should have been enough to disqualify him from running.

Katz told The New York Times that the anger and frustration surrounding Platner's campaign was valid. He said he often criticizes establishment Democrats for not learning from their mistakes, and said, "I think there are things here, many of the critiques that have been made, that are incredibly valid and things to learn from."

Platner ended his Senate campaign in July after Jenny Racicot alleged the Senate candidate had raped her when the two were in a relationship in 2021, which was first reported by Politico.

NEW EXPLOSIVE ALLEGATION ROCKS PLATNER CAMPAIGN STILL REELING FROM RAPE ACCUSATION

"That being said, in hindsight, knowing what we know now, the Reddit posts alone probably should have been enough — or should have been enough. The tattoo should have been enough. The initial New York Times story on troubling behavior should have been enough," Katz said.

Katz's remarks drew some derision online, as those who felt Platner was problematic at the time were roundly dismissed and criticized by the candidate's allies.

"What a bunch of arrogant gaslighters," one wrote on X. "Like there were a ton of us who were literally screaming this from the rooftops and were met with all kinds of name-calling."

Katz was flippant about Platner's Nazi tattoo issue in a profile in The New York Times in January. He was quoted as jokingly asking then-Iowa Democratic Senate hopeful Nathan Sage if he had such a tattoo as well.

The New York Times published a story in June highlighting accounts from several women Platner has dated that referenced unsettling behavior. The story faced scrutiny, as another one of Platner's accusers, Lyndsey Fifield, said the paper tainted her account.

Fifield's account was challenged by some left-wing media figures and politicians because of her past working for Republican organizations. She told Fox News Digital she felt betrayed by how the New York Times handled her allegations in the original report Katz referenced.

Klein asked Katz why he once described Platner's Reddit posts as an asset. CNN unearthed Platner's posts in October 2025 and found the Democratic Senate candidate once described himself as a "communist," wrote that "all" police were bastards and argued that many rural White Americans "actually are" racist and unintelligent.

PLATNER’S THREE-DAY VETTING JOB COMES BACK TO HAUNT DEMS AS RAPE ALLEGATION ROCKS SENATE BID

Additional reporting drew scrutiny to other deleted posts, including one in which Platner appeared to downplay concerns about sexual assault. In one post, Platner wrote that people should "take some responsibility for themselves" and avoid becoming so intoxicated that they end up in compromising situations.

Katz said it was good to see people show Platner some grace to show that he could have changed and evolved since the posts.

"I think that was something we needed, and I don’t want to lose that. I don’t want people’s lesson from this to be that there should never be room for grace. I think that there are a lot of people who have made mistakes or said controversial things who we want to win the support of, who we need to earn the trust of. But I also think I was wrong," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Katz said there was a vetting document about Platner and that it did find a Reddit account, but not the extent of what came out throughout the campaign. Klein noted the post about sexual assault and asked Katz about what he thought hearing the comments now.

"I think it should have been a red line. He talked about it being one of the things he regretted saying the most, that it was indicative of a time of his life when he was lost and angry, and that it was in no way reflective of who he was," Katz said.

Maine Democrats are expected to nominate Troy Jackson this weekend to replace Platner as they try to unseat Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, a key swing vote in the Senate. Collins is seeking a sixth term.

Collins has the distinction of being the only Republican U.S. Senator to represent a state that President Donald Trump lost in all three of his presidential races.

item.title: Bombshell memo shows Biden planned to leave Trump with even more massive immigration crisis
item.description: Sen. Eric Schmitt obtained a Biden White House memo revealing plans to expand TPS to over 3.1 million noncitizens in the administration's final days.
item.content:encoded:
A newly-uncovered Biden White House memo from the administration's final days revealed plans that could have expanded Temporary Protected Status (TPS) to more than 3 million noncitizens while acknowledging that previous court challenges had blocked many of President Donald Trump's efforts to end the protections.

TPS is meant for foreign populations experiencing crises like political unrest or natural disasters, and while Trump has tried to end the "temporary" provisions for Haitians, Nepalese, Salvadorans and Sudanese people, lawsuits from pro-migrant advocates have halted most attempts.

"My investigation uncovered that the Lame Duck Biden White House tried to keep millions of illegal aliens in our country by abusing the 'Temporary' Protected Status program," Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., who acquired the memo, told Fox News Digital on Friday.

"After the American people voted for President Trump’s promise to end the TPS scam, the Biden administration tried to subvert the will of the American people. This was mass amnesty-by-decree. America is for Americans, and it is our home—it is not a permanent refugee camp," he said.

The memo argued that "granting TPS will potentially protect many vulnerable people from President-elect Trump's planned mass deportations... They argue that these protections are likely to hold in court, and they are prepared to litigate efforts to terminate or slow down the implementation of TPS for specified nations by the Trump Administration."

SUPREME COURT WEIGHS TRUMP EFFORT TO TERMINATE TEMPORARY PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIAN, SYRIAN MIGRANTS

"[P]rior federal litigation brought by advocates during the first Trump administration was successful in halting [its] efforts to terminate TPS, though that was due in large part to [its] failure to produce a factual record in support of termination, which is something that could be rectified," the memo went on.

Schmitt said he obtained the memo from Archivist of the United States Edward Forst through his authority as chairman of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on the Constitution.

BIRTH TOURISM COULD SOON CARRY A SEVERE NEW CONSEQUENCE FEW WOULD RISK: 'EXISTENTIAL CRISIS'

"Biden tried to turn TPS into a 3.1-million-person deportation shield, protect Tren de Aragua members, and trap President Trump in years of litigation," he said, adding the move directly betrayed the "will of the people" who ousted liberal Democrats from power the prior election.

"The most disturbing part, Biden's ‘Senior Advisors’ recommended he create 2.1 million NEW TPS designees in the last few weeks of his presidency, despite admitting TPS applications take 6 months," Schmitt added.

"Luckily, that never happened and we have been deporting Ecuadorians and Guatemalans."

TRUMP'S 'THIRD WORLD' TRAVEL BAN COULD BECOME PERMANENT IF FIREBRAND REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER GETS HER WAY

Fox News Digital reached out to Biden and a former Biden official for comment.

Schmitt noted that one week after the January 2025 memo — which he said was erroneously dated "2024" — Biden extended TPS protections for nearly 1 million noncitizens, meaning its transmission still led to "a concrete, mass-migration action."

Schmitt shared a clip of his recent floor remarks on a related topic, where he said the U.S. should not be a "get-rich-quick scheme for the third world" and that Americans don’t try to delay enforcement of squatters on their property in real-life.

The memo reminded Biden he gave TPS protections to Afghans, Cameroonians, Ethiopians, people from Burma, Lebanese, Ukrainians and Venezuelan nationals and repeatedly extended protections for Haitians.

"The previous Administration unsuccessfully attempted to terminate TPS designations for Sudan, Nicaragua, Haiti, El Salvador, Nepal, and Honduras. Courts issued preliminary injunctions blocking the Trump Administration's actions," it read. "Your administration took actions to resolve this litigation by either redesignating Haiti or rescinding the terminations."

The memo noted that Trump had said during the 2024 campaign he intended to revoke TPS protections for Haitians and predicted his incoming administration would likely seek to rescind additional TPS designations.

A chart in the memo estimated potential new TPS eligibility for roughly 1.5 million Guatemalans, 600,000 Ecuadorians, 464,000 Nicaraguans, 455,000 Venezuelans, and smaller populations from Ukraine, Sudan, and Afghanistan — figures Schmitt said totaled more than 3.1 million people.

item.title: Nick Bosa breaks yearslong X hiatus to seemingly celebrate Ryan Clark's ESPN firing
item.description: Nick Bosa broke his four-year silence on X to react to Ryan Clark's ESPN layoff with a single emoji after Clark criticized his MAGA hat in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
After four years off X, Nick Bosa is making up for lost time.

The San Francisco 49ers star edge rusher had not posted on the social media platform since Nov. 12, 2022, aside from just three reposts. That was until Thursday.

The three reposts Bosa had shared included Joe Rogan's 2024 podcast episode with Elon Musk, Michael Bublé promoting a charity, and George Kittle's post from the World Cup final asking for grass instead of turf for NFL stadiums. Ironically, that was the topic of Bosa's last post he wrote himself.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But news that circulated this week was enough for Bosa to get his thumbs going, albeit for an extremely short period of time.

Bosa quoted a post from The Athletic about Ryan Clark being laid off from ESPN, and he made his thoughts relatively clear with just one emoji.

Clark criticized Bosa in the past for wearing a MAGA hat after a game shortly before the 2024 election, which President Donald Trump eventually won.

"It seems very clear to me Nick Bosa understands that when you wear that hat, you take a side," Clark said at the time. "You take a side of division in a sport that’s supposed to bring us together. I’m just waiting for all the people who comment under political and sports things to shut up and dribble or to shut up and play football, to tell him to shut up and rush. But they ain’t going to say it, because they feel the exact same way he do."

Clark recently said that supporting Trump is "more polarizing" than supporting other politicians.

SAQUON BARKLEY 'CAN UNDERSTAND' BACKLASH FOR HIS TRUMP HANGOUT, 'GLAD' GIANTS STARS WORKED OUT DIFFERENCES

"Let’s be honest. Who you supported in 2008, 2012 is nowhere near as polarizing as who you support today," Clark said on his podcast. "[Trump] has clearly picked a side, [and] standing next to him gives the impression that you have to. Which means you stand in direct opposition to the majority of your teammates."

Bosa was fined $11,255 for wearing the hat, but he appeared to have no regrets.

"It was well worth it," Bosa said after the election, before being fined. "I don’t think my position on speaking about it is going to change, so clearly the nation spoke," Bosa added. "We got what we got."

Clark was among several layoffs at the company, including Bart Scott, Tom Pelissero, Karl Ravech, and Cam Newton.
